bmi-calculator.title: BMI Calculator — Calculate Your Body Mass Index
bmi-calculator.description: Calculate your BMI from height and weight. Free, no registration, with interpretation and recommendations.
bmi-calculator.keywords: bmi, body mass index, bmi calculator

faq.a1: BMI (Body Mass Index) is a value that helps assess how well a person's weight matches their height. It is calculated as weight in kilograms divided by height in meters squared.
faq.q2: How accurate is the BMI calculator?
faq.a2: BMI is a rough indicator. It does not account for the ratio of muscle to fat, so athletes may show as "overweight". A body composition analysis is needed for an accurate assessment.
faq.q3: What BMI values are considered normal?
faq.a3: For adults, normal is between 18.5 and 25. Below 18.5 — underweight, 25–30 — overweight, above 30 — obese.

calorie-calculator.title: Calorie Calculator — Calculate Your Daily Intake
calorie-calculator.description: Calculate your daily calorie intake using the Mifflin-St Jeor formula, taking into account age, gender, weight, and activity level.
calorie-calculator.keywords: calories, daily calories, calorie calculator, tdee

faq.a1: The Mifflin-St Jeor formula is used — one of the most accurate formulas for calculating basal metabolic rate.
faq.a2: TDEE (Total Daily Energy Expenditure) is the total number of calories you burn per day, taking physical activity into account.

age-calculator.title: Age Calculator — Calculate Your Exact Age Online
age-calculator.description: Calculate your exact age in years, months, and days from your birth date. Find out how many days you have lived and how many are left until your next birthday.
age-calculator.keywords: age calculator, age by birth date, how old am i

faq.a1: Age is calculated as the difference between the birth date and the target date, broken down into full years, months, and days.
faq.q2: Are leap years taken into account?
faq.a2: Yes, the calculation uses the exact number of days between dates, so leap years are handled automatically.
